turns.text: Before you begin: in your own words, what do you already know about "Reading a limestone cave"?
Limestone is a rock.
Which idea from earlier lessons do you expect to need most here, and why?
Explaining how long it takes.
Hi, I'm Dana. I was told you could help me understand this. I'm starting from zero, so please go slowly.
It fizzes with the acid so the wall is calcite limestone and slightly acidic water dissolves it slowly.
It is about two metres tall and at a growth rate of 0.1 mm a year that makes it roughly twenty thousand years old.
There are crinoid fossils and shells in the wall so this limestone formed on an ancient sea floor.
Where should I start? What's the most important idea I need to get?
Stalactites are made of ice, frozen water I think.
Hold on. You said something that sounded like "stalactites and stalagmites are made of ice or frozen water". If that were true, what would we expect to see? Does that match what you know?
I am not sure.
I'm not sure I follow yet. Can you say a bit more, maybe with an example?
I am not sure.
Maybe look back at the course material from before we started. Is there a part of it that helps here?
I am not sure.
Thank you. I think I could explain some of this to someone else now.
Before you see any feedback: how do you think that went? Which moment are you most satisfied with?
Not great.
What would you do differently if you did it again?
Read the handout again.
